title: Choose the visual world for Artemisa
question: The roll assigned the TV On-Screen Display direction. Keep it, take my pick or the Android TV standard, or re-roll.

options.label: On-Screen Display
options.lineage: TV picture-settings menus, input switchers and broadcast lower-thirds
options.thesis: Your PC is an input on the TV, and Artemisa is its on-screen display.
options.viewport: The focused game's art fills the screen, covers run in one row, and a lower-third bar shows title, host and 4K · 60 · HDR signal badges.
options.risk: Dark ground plus green sits near the old look; it only reads new if selection is a solid green bar and panels stay flat, with no glow.

raised.raise: Everything sits inside the TV's title-safe frame on one fixed grid; nothing floats.
Every screen fits without scrolling: settings tabs cap at seven rows, the quick menu at six.
Neutrals come from one fixed nine-step grey ramp, and in-stream panels slide over the live picture instead of replacing it.
Green appears only on what is selected or live; every other pixel is achromatic.
Focus is physical: the selected tile lifts with scale and a real shadow, never a glow ring.

options.label: Art-led Dashboard
options.lineage: PS5 and Xbox Series home screens
options.thesis: The focused game owns the whole screen; the UI is one row of tiles and a title.
options.viewport: Small tiles run along the top, the focused game's art floods the rest, and its title plus a big Play button sit bottom-left.
options.risk: The most familiar direction: it reads as a console instantly because PS5 and Xbox already ship it, so it says 'console' more than 'Artemisa'.

options.label: Teletext Service
options.thesis: Artemisa as a teletext service: games and settings as numbered pages.
options.viewport: P100 index, each game a numbered row with its page number.
options.case: A controller can't key page numbers, and Shield users don't identify with teletext; loses on both axes.
options.kept: One strict grid inside the TV's title-safe frame.

options.label: Mixtape J-Card
options.thesis: The library as a mixtape: games as tracks on side A and side B.
options.viewport: An unfolded j-card with games listed as tracks.
options.case: Nothing about streaming PC games maps to a tape; loses on both axes.
options.kept: Every screen has to fit its sheet: no scrolling.

options.label: Exposure Record
options.thesis: Settings as translucent sheets stacked over the picture.
options.viewport: Stacked, slightly rotated sheets over a zone wedge.
options.case: The angled sheets fight D-pad focus, and gamers don't know the darkroom; loses on both axes.
options.kept: A fixed tonal ramp as the only greys, and panels sliding over the live picture.

options.label: Iridescent Cloud Edge
options.thesis: An achromatic field with colour only at the active edge.
options.viewport: White screen, pastel band on the focused tile.
options.case: A white TV UI in a dark room is glaring, and the pastels drop the required green; loses on both axes.
options.kept: Colour reserved strictly for the active element.

options.label: Leather Studio
options.thesis: Games as boxed objects on a stitched-leather shelf.
options.viewport: A wooden shelf of game cases under a leather header.
options.case: Heavy textures fight the key art and read as dated; loses on both axes.
options.kept: The active item physically lifts, with a true shadow.

options.label: Cloud Quarry
options.thesis: Menus cut from blocks of weather.
options.viewport: A cloud cliff with games cut into it.
options.case: No relationship to game streaming; loses on both axes.
options.kept: Panels move with weight: a short slide and settle, never a fade in place.

canonCard.label: Android TV standard
canonCard.thesis: Google TV / Leanback browse rows, executed cleanly with the Artemisa green.
canonCard.viewport: A left rail (Home, Library, Settings) beside rows of cards with a featured banner on top.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every Android TV app, by design.
